definitions.explanation: A situation in which one good result produces the conditions for the next, so improvement feeds on itself. Standard vocabulary in economic and business commentary.

examples.japanese: {経済|けいざい}の{好|こう}{循環|じゅんかん}が{生|う}まれた。
examples.english: A virtuous cycle has emerged in the economy.

examples.japanese: {賃上|ちんあ}げと{消費|しょうひ}の{好|こう}{循環|じゅんかん}を{目指|めざ}す。
examples.english: We are aiming for a virtuous cycle of wage increases and consumption.

examples.japanese: {社員|しゃいん}の{満足度|まんぞくど}が{上|あ}がればサービスの{質|しつ}も{上|あ}がるという{好|こう}{循環|じゅんかん}に{入|はい}っている。
examples.english: We have entered a virtuous cycle in which higher employee satisfaction raises the quality of service.

notes:
COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {好|こう}{循環|じゅんかん}を{生|う}む: to create a virtuous cycle
- {好|こう}{循環|じゅんかん}に{入|はい}る: to enter a virtuous cycle
- {好|こう}{循環|じゅんかん}が{回|まわ}り{始|はじ}める: for the cycle to start turning

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {悪|あく}{循環|じゅんかん}: vicious cycle — the far more frequently used of the pair, and the word to learn first.

USAGE:
Mostly written and formal: economics reporting, policy statements, and business planning. In casual speech people describe the same idea with いい{流|なが}れ (a good run of things).
